bug_description.original: Heap-buffer-overflow in pcpp::IPv6Address::IPv6Address OSS-Fuzz report: https://bugs.chromium.org/p/oss-fuzz/issues/detail?id=432892652 Crash type: Heap-buffer-overflow READ 16 Crash state: pcpp::IPv6Address::IPv6Address pcpp::SomeIpSdIPv6Option::getIpAddress readParsedPacket
bug_description.normalized: The saved PoC is accepted as SOME/IP-SD by project code, then the parser reads attacker-controlled option metadata from the packet buffer. In `isDataValid()`, the options-length field is loaded from `data + sizeof(someipsdhdr) + sizeof(uint32_t) + getLenEntries(data)`, but the final check compares `dataLen` only with that raw length value and not with the options field offset plus that length. The constructed `SomeIpSdLayer` therefore exposes an options section whose declared layout can describe an IPv6 option near the end of the backing packet. `getOptions()` computes the options base `offset`, reads `hdr->type`, and calls `parseOption(optionType, offset)` before validating that the selected record has the full byte extent required for an IPv6 option object. For IPv6 option types, `parseOption()` constructs `SomeIpSdIPv6Option(this, offset)`, whose constructor sets `m_DataLen = sizeof(someipsdhdroptionsipv6)`. The option keeps the same `SomeIpSdLayer` data container and offset, so `getDataPtr()` later returns `m_Data + offset`. `SomeIpSdIPv6Option::getIpAddress()` casts that pointer to `someipsdhdroptionsipv6*` and passes `hdr->ipv6Address` to `IPv6Address`; that constructor copies 16 bytes. The saved ASan trace confirms the resulting heap-buffer-overflow read in `IPv6Address::IPv6Address -> SomeIpSdIPv6Option::getIpAddress`, with the fuzz helper only invoking the accessor.

source.description: Project parser admission reads the attacker-controlled SOME/IP-SD options-length field. In this witness, the top-level dataLen check admits the packet even though the later selected IPv6 option record has too few bytes for a full IPv6 option object.
source.value_from: The PoC bytes are the `data` buffer. This expression reads the 32-bit options-length field at the packet-derived offset immediately after the SOME/IP-SD header and entry section.

root_cause.description: Safety obligation violation. `getOptions()` constructs an option from `optionType` and `offset` before any source statement verifies that the selected record has `sizeof(someipsdhdroptionsipv6)` bytes available for an IPv6 option object.

sink.description: Sink. `getIpAddress()` consumes the same option backing pointer by casting `getDataPtr()` to `someipsdhdroptionsipv6*` and passing `hdr->ipv6Address` to `IPv6Address`, whose constructor copies 16 bytes.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerable parser state originates when project code reads the PoC-controlled options-length field from the SOME/IP-SD payload and uses it in an incomplete admission check.

parser_admitted.description: Sample-specific SOME/IP-SD gate: the PoC must satisfy this predicate so the buffer is accepted as SOME/IP-SD. The last comparison only checks `dataLen` against the raw 32-bit options-length field read from the packet, not against the options section's true end offset inside the buffer.

admitted_location.code: return new SomeIpSdLayer(data, dataLen, prevLayer, packet);

fine_trace.note: Source. The project admission predicate reads the PoC-controlled SOME/IP-SD options-length field. In this witness, the top-level dataLen check admits the packet even though the later selected IPv6 option record has too few bytes for a full someipsdhdroptionsipv6 object.

fine_trace.code: uint32_t lenOption = be16toh(*((uint16_t *)(m_Data + offsetOption + len))) + 3 * sizeof(uint8_t);
fine_trace.note: After admission, the parser reads an attacker-controlled per-option length from `m_Data` at the current option cursor and materializes it as the declared option span `lenOption`.
`countOptions()` advances the consumed-option cursor by the declared span without checking that this particular option record fits in the real remaining packet bytes.

fine_trace.code: size_t offset = sizeof(someipsdhdr) + sizeof(uint32_t) + getLenEntries() + sizeof(uint32_t);
fine_trace.note: `getOptions()` recomputes the project-code options base in the same `m_Data` buffer, so subsequent option objects point into the admitted packet at `m_Data + offset`.

Root cause. The parser calls `parseOption(optionType, offset)` and may construct an IPv6 option before any source statement proves that the bytes at the selected `offset` cover a full `someipsdhdroptionsipv6` object.
For IPv6 option types, `parseOption()` constructs `SomeIpSdIPv6Option(this, offset)` using only the data container and offset; it still receives no available-byte bound.
The constructed IPv6 option records a logical option length of `sizeof(someipsdhdroptionsipv6)`, so its accessors treat the backing pointer as a complete IPv6 option structure.

Project-code propagation. The IPv6 option keeps the `SomeIpSdLayer` as `m_DataContainer` and the selected `offset` as `m_Offset`, so `getDataPtr()` resolves to the same packet backing pointer `m_Data + offset`.

Sink. `getIpAddress()` casts that same option data pointer to `someipsdhdroptionsipv6*` and passes `hdr->ipv6Address` to `IPv6Address`; the constructor then copies 16 bytes, which the saved ASan trace reports as the overflowing read. The harness frame is only the caller that invokes this project accessor.

cross_validation.fixed_result: The saved fixed-commit trace is clean for the same PoC, matching repair_decision.json.
cross_validation.repair_decision: repair_decision.json records that commit 25e1f9cb is the true fix for this PoC and that the vulnerable first-known-bad commit reproduces the crash.

poc.trigger: The testcase must be parsed as a packet whose UDP payload is accepted as SOME/IP-SD and whose project-code options traversal constructs `SomeIpSdIPv6Option(this, offset)` for a truncated option record; invoking `getIpAddress()` then copies from `hdr->ipv6Address` past the packet allocation.

format.name: OSS-Fuzz pcap/pcapng testcase
format.contract: The witness proves the saved testcase reaches project code that exposes a malformed SOME/IP-SD IPv6 option object backed by insufficient bytes. The fuzz helper is only the caller that invokes the accessor; the vulnerability logic is the project parser constructing and later reading that option without a full-object extent check.
